_comment: API that is suppressed from generation and then exposed by hand.
A generator writes a map of what it generated, so a member it was told to skip is absent even
though the shipped package has it. Documentation reads these maps to decide whether a backticked
term is an API name at all, so without an entry here a real name a reader can type is
indistinguishable from a typo.
This folder is not a platform. The loader reads every directory under the api-map root and keys
forward answers by the platform field on each name, so one file answers for all of them -- which
is what these entries need, being members whose only spelling difference is house casing.
One entry serves both directions: the canonical name with a platform spelling gives the forward
answer for that platform and the reverse answer for the spelling.
Each entry records where the hand-written exposure actually lives, because that is the only
evidence that the name is real. If one of these is ever generated normally, the generated map
wins on agreement and this entry should be deleted rather than left to rot.
Points carries [TSSuppressWidgetMember] on the web branch and [WFSuppressWidgetMember] on the
other, so no generated map has it. The web spelling is not a guess: the hand-written wrapper
ig_-shapefile-record.template.ts declares `get points(): Point[][]`, which agrees with the
[ClientName("points")] on the field. On the XAML platforms the field is plainly public and keeps
its own name. Its siblings FieldValues and Bounds are generated, and Blazor spells those
PascalCase, so Points is what Blazor calls this one.
The whole *MarkerTemplate family on SeriesViewer is suppressed on every platform at once --
[WFSuppressWidgetMember] through [JAVASuppressWidgetMember] -- so not one of them appears in any
generated map. The suppression keeps them off the component wrapper, not off the class: the web
SeriesViewer declares `get checkmarkMarkerTemplate(): DataTemplate`.
Only the checkmark template is recorded here, because it is the only one a topic names. This is
also the newest of them, which is why refreshing the maps did not help.
A type rather than a member, and absent for a different reason: it is internal with [WFWidget]
in the shipping build, which marks it for WinForms and says nothing to the web translator, and
it reaches the web packages by being exported rather than by being wrapped --
public_api.DV.Shared.GEO.JS.ts exports it under its own name.
Named identically everywhere, so this entry exists to say the name is real rather than to
translate it. Marking the class [Widget] would let the generator record it and make this entry
unnecessary; that is a product-source decision, not one to take from the documentation side.
